intro: Lesson 1: What causes waves and tides? (4.1). To understand how wind makes waves and how the Moon causes tides

picture.alt: Atlantic waves at Fistral Beach, Cornwall
picture.draw: Draw and label: Wave diagram sheet

questions.q: Explain why some waves are bigger than others.
questions.a: Stronger wind, blowing for longer, over a longer fetch makes bigger waves
questions.model: Three factors: wind speed, how long it blows, and fetch. Cornwall: strong winds over a long Atlantic fetch. So bigger waves.

questions.a: Water flowing back down the beach
Mainly the pull of the Moon's gravity (and the Sun's)

questions.q: Core: Draw labelled diagrams of a constructive and a destructive wave, showing swash and backwash.
questions.a: Constructive: long low wave, big swash arrow, small backwash. Destructive: tall steep wave, small swash, big backwash
questions.model: Teacher shows it first: a low, long wave, a long arrow up the beach labelled 'strong swash', a short arrow back labelled 'weak backwash'.

questions.q: Extend: In the portal response box, explain the difference between spring and neap tides.
questions.a: Spring tides (new and full Moon) have the highest high and lowest low tides because the Sun and Moon pull together; neap tides (half Moon) have the smallest range

questions.q: Stretch: Why might destructive waves be more common in winter?
questions.a: Winter storms bring stronger winds, making bigger, steeper waves
The distance the wind blows over open water

questions.q: Big question: why is the sea never still?
questions.a: Wind makes waves all the time, and the Moon's gravity makes tides rise and fall
